mappings.label: HVAC — heat pump heating (daily energy)
mappings.notes: Bryant/Carrier daily energy component hPHeat -> channel_id 'hpheat' (PLAN.md §7.2), metrics kwh_day and cost_day_usd at LOCAL midnight of the measured day. Physically this is the Bryant 284ANV060000 5-ton outdoor unit on Panel B slots 10/12 (blackstart B-10-12). Deliberately NOT joined with blackstart_device_id: this row is a cloud-reported energy component, not the breaker channel, and giving it the breaker's identity would invite double counting against a future leviton breaker_p10 row.

mappings.label: HVAC — blower fan during gas heat (daily energy)
mappings.notes: Component fanGas. Expected structurally absent on this house: energyConfig.fangas is disabled, so PLAN.md §7.2 emits no rows at all (not zeros). Mapped anyway so that a row which ever does appear arrives with a label instead of as an unmapped channel.

mappings.label: HVAC — gas heat (daily energy)
mappings.notes: Component gas. Expected disabled (heat pump + electric strips, no gas). PLAN.md §7.2: if gasKwh is ever enabled AND nonzero it is recorded verbatim under metric kwh_day and WARNed — the field name says kWh but gas almost certainly is not kWh. Do not read this channel's kwh_day as electricity without checking that warning.

mappings.label: Bryant Evolution system — outdoor temp, mode, stage
mappings.notes: 30s status channel (PLAN.md §7.3). Metrics: outdoor_temp_f (system oat), mode and stage (unit='enum', integer codes from the append-only tables in sources/bryant.py — decode is in the Glue column comment for `value`). 'stage' comes from the OUTDOOR unit's opstat only (DEVIATIONS.md #58) and may be permanently empty if this unit reports a capacity percentage instead of a word (#59).

mappings.label: Bryant Evolution zone 1 — thermostat
mappings.notes: 30s status channel (PLAN.md §7.3). Metrics: indoor_temp_f (rt), humidity_pct (rh), setpoint_heat_f (htsp), setpoint_cool_f (clsp), fan (enum). channel_id comes from the API's own zone id, and only zones reporting enabled=='on' emit rows (DEVIATIONS.md #66). How many zones this system actually has is UNCONFIRMED until a live status poll runs (DEVIATIONS.md #75.6) — run `energycap discover`, then add zone_2… here if it reports more.

REAL — confirmed by `energycap discover` 2026-08-17. Hub 1000_0046_1D52 is the panel Leviton names 'Panel A'; the identification is not a guess about the letter, it is two independent label matches: this breaker reports name 'Water Heater' at position 19 and blackstart A-19-21 is 'Water heater' on slots 19/21, and breaker_p23 matches A-23-25 the same way. Carries no label/category of its own on purpose — with blackstart_device_id set and no explicit override, montfort.json supplies label/panel/slots/category/priority/estimated_watts, which is PLAN.md §9's rule that blackstart stays the source of truth for labels. 2-pole LB230-0ST, so ONE channel named for the lower slot; slots render as "19,21". Observed drawing 2462 W (element on) and 0 W (idle) within one hour — a resistive element holds a constant wattage while heating, so a long run of identical values here is real, not a stuck reading.

REAL — confirmed by discover 2026-08-17. Leviton name 'Mud Room Air Conditioner' at position 23; blackstart A-23-25 is 'Mini-split — mud room addition' on slots 23/25. Label comes from blackstart (the more accurate of the two — it is a mini-split, not a window AC). 2-pole LB220-0ST, observed 103-201 W.

mappings.label: Panel A service feed (leg A)
mappings.notes: REAL — discover 2026-08-17 reports usageType GRID_POWER on hub 1000_0046_1D52 channel 1. This is the whole-panel feed, so it is the denominator every per-circuit number should be compared against; it is NOT a blackstart device (no breaker occupies it) and therefore carries explicit fields only. Do not sum this with the breaker channels below it — that double counts.

mappings.label: HVAC subpanel feeder (leg A) — electric strip heat
mappings.notes: REAL — discover 2026-08-17. Leviton reports usageType HEAT_PUMP on this clamp pair, and THAT LABEL IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE — it is a dropdown someone picked in the app, which is why the label is overridden here (PLAN.md §9's explicit-override rule). What the clamps are physically on is the feeder to the HVAC subpanel, which blackstart B-6-8 describes as 'Feed-through lug tap — feeds the HVAC subpanel'; that subpanel holds the KFCEH3301C20 20 kW heat kit, i.e. the ELECTRIC STRIPS, not the compressor. The 5-ton Bryant 284ANV060000 outdoor unit is a separate circuit (blackstart B-10-12) and is not metered by this pair. Evidence: observed a flat 0 W across 17 minutes of continuous cooling with the blower running and the compressor at 35% capacity — the compressor's power was demonstrably not passing through these clamps. UNVERIFIED: the subpanel has not been opened, so this is a strong inference from the inventory plus the observed behaviour, not confirmed wiring. Expect this channel to read ~0 all summer and to carry real load only during defrost, aux heat and deep winter. A future breaker_p10 row (compressor) is the channel to correlate with cooling, NOT this one.
